items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: I remember Rod Kless, your old clarinetist on that Bluebird band that you had, the Ragtime band

ctx.x: He was a timid soul. He was very nice. I liked his planet playing very much. I believe he used to, you'd think he was afraid of a microphone. And Joe Oliver, he was afraid of a microphone too. He didn't like a microphone. Really? Didn't like? I don't either.

You wouldn't know it because you recorded so much and it sounds great. I remember Rod Kless, your old clarinetist on that Bluebird band that you had, the Ragtime band, told me once he studied a little bit, actually took a couple lessons from Dodds, I think. He used to go down and actually practically study with him, if not actual formal lessons, at least get ideas from him to his home, I think, to study.

Well, we all used to go down on the Southside and listen to all those bands. Chicago at that time was just full of good bands. It was in a place you could go that you wouldn't hear a good band. You had Freddie Kepler, Jimmy Noon. That's when Zutty was in his prime. And Sid Catler was just coming up then. Yeah.
